title: Evaluating the Impact of Local Differential Privacy on Utility Loss via Influence Functions
reasoning: The paper's core motivation and problem statement are deeply rooted in ethical considerations surrounding data privacy, user consent, and the trade-off between privacy and utility in real-world data collection and model deployment. It discusses the challenge of selecting privacy parameters (epsilon) to ensure a 'meaningful degree of privacy' without 'significantly degrading the utility,' which is an explicit ethical balancing act. The paper provides an example of a company using end-user data, and the ethical implications of publishing or selling models trained on such data, requiring privatization for 'concerned end-users'. This goes beyond a brief 'ethical considerations' section, forming a central part of the research's 'why'.
